scope: Only the two accepted Chapter20 aggregate actions. Plotting does not reconstruct firm identities, fit posteriors, choose boundaries or rerun the historical consumer.

source.attribution: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024) supplied separate scalar report cards and baseline inputs; these common race-gender actions are an analyst-constructed extension.

orientation: Larger signed targets have higher reported priority; grade1 is highest and lies at the left of a ribbon.
family: Two archived contiguous cut patterns on the same reconstructed weighted-row-sum order; both have an at-most-four nonempty-grade cap.
coefficient_convention: Historical completion: retain raw upper-triangle strict-superiority entries and replace the opposite entry by its complement. Error coefficients follow the completed reverse entry. This is not a validated exact weak-event posterior law.
precision: Sizes, N and M are integers. Coefficient-error sums retain the finite decimal tokens from the accepted array reevaluation. Printed disclosure/error fractions use three decimals and risk four; these are coefficient-based conditional summaries, not observed error rates or calibrated posterior guarantees.
limits: Do not invent names, firm identities, posterior intervals or assignments from these aggregates.
Two tau values define different losses; their risk difference is not common-loss improvement or deterioration.
Two archived actions are not a frontier or an optimality certificate.
Marginal race/gender arrays suffice only for this additive expected criterion-error calculation; no composite or simultaneous-correctness claim.
The current accepted read-only reconstruction pins source arrays, but does not establish every detail of the original-run environment.
